# F3 · Transfer and substitution calls

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F3-AC-01` – `F3-UP-07`.
Load alongside this file: `ENGINE.criteria.md`.

#### F3 · Transfer and substitution calls

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Must.** The core weekly transfer and lineup decisions Section 2.1 names first. |
| Serves | The first core job in Section 2.3 — the transfer and lineup decisions. |
| Happy path | The manager opens the Assistant, sees each recommended change as a card, opens one, compares the two players on a single evaluation table, reads the reasoning, and accepts, rejects or stores it. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F3-AC-01** | Every call has exactly one of three states: pending review (default), selected, or rejected. |
| **F3-AC-02** | Decisions are held per call, not per category — accepting one of two transfer calls leaves the other pending. |
| **F3-AC-03** | **A substitution call has three shapes, not one:** a *forced* swap (an unplayable starter has to come out), a *doubt* swap (a flagged starter for a fit bench player), and a **bench-order** call — reordering the outfield bench so the right player is first in line for an auto-substitution. |
| **F3-AC-04** | A bench-order call has no starting-eleven pair: its two sides are the two bench players whose order changes, its net is the difference in their effective points multiplied by the probability an auto-sub fires for the slot they cover, and its cost is £0.00. |
| **F3-AC-05** | A bench-order call uses the same head-to-head layout, master evaluation rows and gestures as every other call, and stays inside the substitution category rather than becoming a fourth. |
| **F3-AC-06** | **In a blank gameweek the bench-order call is the most important substitution rather than the least**, because an auto-substitution is the only cover a blanking starter has — and if the bench blanks too there is nothing to cover with. The Overview editorial must state that consequence in a blank week (F8-AC-07), not leave it to be inferred from the call's position in the list. |
| **F3-AC-07** | Swipe right selects (adding to the week's shortlist), swipe left rejects (it will not resurface this week), swipe up leaves it pending. |
| **F3-AC-08** | The same three actions are drawn as tappable tiles under the card, so the gesture model is visible rather than described. |
| **F3-AC-09** | There is no separate remove or delete action; rejecting is the removal mechanism. |
| **F3-AC-10** | A decision can be changed at any time from the overview card's decision panel, without reopening the detail card. |
| **F3-AC-11** | A rejected card stays visible at reduced opacity with its decision panel, so an accidental reject is two taps from correction. There is no undo toast. |
| **F3-AC-12** | Deciding a call advances to the next undecided call in that category; when none are left the tab meta reads *Done* and Category cleared is shown. |
| **F3-AC-13** | Head to head shows only undecided calls. There is no way to browse back to a decided one from inside this screen; that happens from the overview or from Category cleared instead. |
| **F3-AC-14** | **On Category cleared every decided row is a two-way control.** Tapping a row returns that call to pending review; tapping it again restores the decision it had. |
| **F3-AC-15** | Category cleared's line beneath the list reports the live state rather than describing the gesture — "tap a decision to change it" when nothing is reopened, "1 call reopened · tap again to put it back" once something is. A label that promises an interaction has to perform one. |
| **F3-AC-16** | The evaluation table uses one master row list — availability, form, projected points this gameweek, this gameweek's fixtures, price, selected-by, season points, transfers in, transfers out, with a *games this gameweek* row inserted at the top in a blank or double week (defined once in 3.1, Head to head) — in the same order, identical on transfer, substitution and captain calls. There are no per-category bespoke rows, and the stat table uses the same list as its columns. |
| **F3-AC-17** | **Each call carries at most one flag, and Forced outranks Watch.** *Forced* is red and is a property of the call (3.4 Constraints). *Watch* is amber and is set by code when the inputs the call rests on are about to move — realised price movement trending toward a change tonight for a player on either side, or a press conference due before the deadline for a club in the call. |
| **F3-AC-18** | Neither flag is ever derived from conviction, and neither changes the figure. The Watch flag reads *WATCH* with no qualifier, because the reason is one tap away on the detail card and a longer flag squeezes the call's title. |
| **F3-AC-19** | Each evaluation row highlights the winning side: the winning value is set in a green pill (background, text and border), not merely marked by the chevron beside it. The losing value stays plain, uncoloured text. |
| **F3-AC-20** | A tie is legitimate and renders distinctly: neither side gets the green pill, and the row's mark is neutral rather than a chevron. |
| **F3-AC-21** | The card fills the screen exactly. The versus band, summary strip, reasoning block and swipe tiles are fixed; the evaluation table absorbs the remaining height and is the only scrolling region. |
| **F3-AC-22** | Reasoning is clamped to four lines and may reference only dimensions present in the table. |
| **F3-AC-23** | On a transfer call only, either side can be changed from a curated list — three outgoing candidates, five incoming. Substitution and captaincy calls have no picker; their pairs are fixed by the squad. |
| **F3-AC-24** | Selecting a candidate recomputes every row winner, the net projected points, the conviction percentage and band, the cost, the NBal and the reasoning line. |
| **F3-AC-25** | Cost applies to transfers only. It is the incoming player's price minus the outgoing player's **selling** price — for a player already owned, FPL's selling price is the purchase price plus half of any profit since, rounded down, which can be below his current price. |
| **F3-AC-26** | Purchase prices are therefore stored per player (3.5). |
| **F3-AC-27** | **NBal** (3.1 Terms) is the Balance minus the cost of the calls in scope — the manager's selected calls in the Assistant status bar, the displayed filter's scenario in the squad widget. It may go negative, and must be shown as negative rather than blocked. |
| **F3-AC-28** | **A substitution costs nothing.** No money moves and no transfer is used, so its cost reads £0.00 — never a difference between two prices the manager already owns. The same holds for a captaincy call (F4), since one shared summary strip serves all three categories. |
| **F3-AC-29** | Selecting a call updates the shortlist count, the status bar's NBal, the selected filter's scenario and the priority tally. |
| **F3-AC-30** | **How this was calculated is one tap away.** An expandable section on the card surfaces each side's raw projected points from the feed, the availability and rotation multipliers with their source (FPL's own figure, or the model's rating with its quoted evidence), the resulting net, the k value used, and any trust-factor haircuts applied. |
| **F3-AC-31** | Nothing is calculated inside that breakdown — every value already exists in the pipeline — so a conviction figure that looks wrong can be traced to the layer that produced it rather than guessed at. |
| **F3-AC-32** | **The fixtures row carries the three-bar strip specified in F1-AC-19**, not just this week's pill: this week's fixture pill, then a bar each for the following two, coloured by difficulty. A transfer is scored over three gameweeks, and this gives the manager that horizon without inventing a fourth figure the reasoning-may-only-cite-the-table rule would also have to accommodate. |
| **F3-AC-33** | Substitution and captain/vice calls show the same fixtures row for consistency, even though they are scored on this gameweek alone. |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F3-UP-01** | **The accepted set costs more than the bank holds.** Acceptance: stated at plan level, never silently drawn. The Assistant status bar's NBal goes red; a red marker sits beside the squad widget and opens a panel naming the breach in numbers ("spends £0.2m more than you have. Drop one, or fund it with a downgrade elsewhere"). Proposing the fix automatically is out of scope. |
| **F3-UP-02** | **The accepted set uses more transfers than the free-transfer allowance.** Acceptance: not blocked, but stated. The squad widget's free-transfer chip turns red and states the deduction in plain terms (for example "FT 2/1 · −4 pts"), and the scenario's projected-points total is net of that hit, so the cost of the extra change is visible in the same figure the manager is judging the plan by. How the hit is attributed — to the specific call that caused it, and therefore to that call's conviction, or only to the scenario total — is not specified. |
| **F3-UP-03** | **The accepted set breaks an FPL squad rule** — more than three players from one club, or an illegal shape. Acceptance: the same scenario-validation panel names each breach with its numbers ("LIV 4/3 · FPL allows three from one club"), club counts derive from the actual fifteen, and every filter chip carries the same marker for its own scenario so an unimplementable plan is visible without switching to it. |
| **F3-UP-04** | **Two calls would touch the same player.** Acceptance: this is prevented at generation, not detected in the interface. The week is generated as one plan; a substitution that benches a player and a transfer that sells him are never both produced. The constraint is re-checked on every refresh, and scenario totals therefore cannot double-count. |
| **F3-UP-05** | **There is nothing worth changing.** Acceptance: no advice is manufactured to fill the screen. The editorial says so and says why ("your fifteen is fit, nobody's fixtures have turned, hold your free transfer"), the call count reads none, the tally is empty, Before and After are identical, and each category states that it is clear. A quiet week is a legitimate answer and must read as a decision, not an empty list. |
| **F3-UP-06** | **The manager rejects every call.** Acceptance: accepted as a legitimate answer with no special acknowledgement screen — every card carries its rejected state, the selected scenario is the unchanged squad, and each category reads Done. Refresh remains the way to ask again. |
| **F3-UP-07** | **No legal substitution exists** — every bench player is injured or doubtful. Acceptance: parked. The honest "no good option" verdict is agreed in principle but not built in the first version; until it is, the category carries no substitution call. |
